# NBK Policy Pressure Score

A read-only dashboard and replication package for one indicator: the **policy pressure score** for National Bank of Kazakhstan (NBK) base-rate decisions.

## The indicator

| | |
|---|---|
| **Value** | Policy pressure score = P(Increase) − P(Decrease) from an ordered logit on six factors (inflation, exports, imports, corporate lending, household lending, consumption). |
| **Unit** | Probability difference, from −1 (a cut is certain) to +1 (a hike is certain); 0 means balanced. |
| **Period** | One value per NBK base-rate decision date. Factor values are taken from the calendar month two months before the decision month (an assumption; see Limitations). |
| **Latest** | -0.306 for the decision of 2026-10-27 (95% delta-method band -0.747 to +0.136), a change of -0.112 from the previous decision. |
| **Next decision** | Increase 8.1% · Hold 53.2% · Decrease 38.7%. Both upcoming rounds use the latest factor values, so their probabilities are identical. Meeting dates come from `config/forecast_rounds.json`. |

**Main result (ratio below 1, but not distinguishable from Always Hold).** Ordered logit meets the pre-specified criterion against Always Hold on the holdout (RMSE ratio 0.995, below 1). This does not show that the model forecasts better. The 95% block-bootstrap interval for the RMSE ratio (0.780 to 1.335) contains 1, and the Diebold–Mariano test (HLN-corrected) gives p = 0.961, so on 18 holdout decisions the model cannot be distinguished from Always Hold in either direction. Effect of the data update (OLD = git tag before-data-update-2026-09-07, NEW = current files): usable decisions 88 → 89; estimation sample 70 → 71 decisions (ending 2024-06-03 → 2024-07-15); holdout 18 → 18 decisions (2024-07-15–2026-09-07 → 2024-09-02–2026-10-27). The holdout RMSE ratio changed from 1.002 to 0.995, so the pre-specified rule's label changed from "does not meet the pre-specified criterion (RMSE ratio not below 1)" to "meets the pre-specified criterion (RMSE ratio below 1)". 95% bootstrap intervals: OLD 0.828 to 1.230, NEW 0.780 to 1.335; both ratios lie inside both intervals, so the change does not show that the model forecasts better or worse than before. The model's holdout RMSE is 0.620 against 0.624 for Always Hold, on 18 decisions from 2024-09-02 to 2026-10-27. Household lending is the only slope that is significant after Holm adjustment (raw p 0.008, Holm p 0.047). In "Differenced non-stationary factors" (RB09, `outputs/robustness_table.md`) its coefficient is 0.3651 (raw p 0.201, Holm p 0.452): the only significant factor loses significance when its non-stationarity is removed.

**Probability scoring (RPS).** Supplementary measure (exploratory, added after the holdout had been seen; the pre-specified verdict stays RMSE-based): the ranked probability score on the same holdout (lower is better) is 0.154 for the model, 0.194 for Always Hold and 0.159 for the class frequencies of the estimation sample. Simple class frequencies do almost as well as the model, so the six factors add little beyond the base rates of cuts, holds and hikes; most of the gain over Always Hold comes from admitting that cuts and hikes happen.

**Robustness is mixed.** A check "survives" when all six slope signs match the main model and the benchmark conclusion is the same. Of the 9 checks, 8 are comparable with the main score; RB03 is not (binary Increase-vs-not target: it cannot predict a decrease, and its P(Increase) is compared with a −1/0/+1 score) and is left out of the counts. Checks that survive: 1 of 8 (RB04). The RMSE ratio is below 1 on the check's own holdout in 6 of 8 (RB01, RB04, RB05, RB07, RB08, RB09); the benchmark conclusion differs from the main result in 2 (RB02, RB06). Each check uses its own holdout, so their RMSE ratios are not directly comparable.

The largest contributions to the latest change come from household lending (-0.046), corporate lending (-0.037) and exports (-0.016).

## Install
### Quick start (one command, no virtual environment)

Step 1. Open a terminal inside the project folder. The folder must contain `run.py`, `README.md`, `requirements.txt`, `src/`, `tests/` and `data/raw/`.

- Windows: open the project folder in File Explorer, click the address bar at the top, type `powershell` and press Enter. A terminal opens already in the right folder.
- VS Code (any system): File -> Open Folder -> choose the project folder, then Terminal -> New Terminal.
- macOS: right-click the folder -> New Terminal at Folder.

Check that you are in the right place: `dir` (Windows) or `ls` (macOS/Linux) must list `run.py` and `requirements.txt`.

Step 2. Run one command.

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
py -m pip install -r requirements.txt; py run.py
```

macOS / Linux / Git Bash:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt && python run.py
```

The dashboard opens in the browser at http://localhost:8503. It works offline: it reads the saved CSV files in `data/`, downloads nothing and needs no API key. No virtual environment is needed, so there is nothing to activate. If `py` is not found, use `python` instead of `py`. Python 3.13 or 3.14 is recommended (3.11 or newer is required).

After the first installation you only need `py run.py` (or `python run.py`) to start the dashboard again.

### Alternative: isolated virtual environment
Tested on Python 3.14 (Windows) and 3.13 (Linux). Run from the repository root.

**Windows (PowerShell):**

<!-- install-steps:windows:start -->
```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv\Scripts\python.exe run.py
```
<!-- install-steps:windows:end -->

**macOS / Linux:**

<!-- install-steps:posix:start -->
```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python run.py
```
<!-- install-steps:posix:end -->

Run these commands from the repository root (the folder that contains run.py), not from your home folder. Activation is not needed: the commands call the virtual-environment Python directly, so Windows' script-execution policy (the 'running scripts is disabled' error for Activate.ps1) does not apply. If `python` is not found on Windows, use `py` instead of `python` in the first line. To use the environment interactively you may activate it (`.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` on Windows, `source .venv/bin/activate` elsewhere), but nothing here depends on it.

## Run the site

```text
python run.py
```

This one command starts the dashboard at <http://localhost:8503> and opens a browser tab (`--port N` to change the port, `--no-browser` to stay in the terminal). `make` is optional; every Makefile target just calls `run.py`. The app only reads `data/processed/` and `model/artifact.json`; it never fits a model. When the calendar source cannot be reached within two seconds, the page shows a **CACHED DATA** label and keeps serving the local files.

## Regenerate all outputs

```text
python run.py data      # rebuild data/processed/ from data/raw/
python run.py model     # re-estimate; rewrites model/artifact.json and the annexes in outputs/
python run.py robust    # exploratory stress tests -> model/robust_eval.json, outputs/robust_evaluation.md
python run.py report    # tables, figures and numbers for the note, then this README
python run.py facts     # validate docs/facts_to_fill.* and regenerate SOURCES.md, provenance, card, rule, validity facts
python run.py all       # data, model, robust, report, facts, then the tests
```

`python run.py report` writes `outputs/results_table.md`, `outputs/oos_comparison.md`, `outputs/economic_size.md`, `outputs/robustness_table_short.md`, `outputs/fig_history.png`, `outputs/fig_oos.png`, `outputs/fig_contributions.png` and `outputs/numbers_for_note.json`. Each entry in the numbers file has a `source` field that points to the artifact field it came from.

Facts that only a person can supply (publishers, URLs, retrieval dates, real release lags, the origin and status of the indicator, the named user) go into `docs/facts_to_fill.csv` and `docs/facts_to_fill.md`. `python run.py facts` validates them (dates must be `YYYY-MM-DD` and not in the future; lags must be whole days) and regenerates `data/raw/SOURCES.md`, `data/processed/provenance.json` (shown in the dashboard), `outputs/release_lag_check.md`, `docs/indicator_card.md`, `docs/decision_rule.md` and `docs/validity_facts.md`. The release-lag check compares the assumed offset in `config/release_lag.json` with the real lags; it never changes the estimation.

### Exploratory stress tests (added in review, after the holdout had been seen)

`python run.py robust` (`src/robust_eval.py`) leaves the main model and its verdict untouched and asks how far the verdict can be trusted. It reports a moving-block bootstrap interval and a Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold-corrected Diebold–Mariano test for the holdout RMSE ratio; the ranked probability score (RPS), a proper score for ordered probability forecasts that, unlike the log score, is finite for Always Hold; a rolling-origin, one-step-ahead evaluation inside the estimation sample, which uses no holdout data and is the fair basis for comparing specifications; two alternative specifications motivated by policy-rule reasoning (the NBK's previous decision, the ex-post real rate and the recent change in inflation) and a ridge-penalized version of the main model whose penalty is chosen at every forecast origin from earlier decisions only; and a raw-data anomaly screen (modified z-scores of monthly changes) that flags source values worth re-checking. Results are in `outputs/robust_evaluation.md` and in the Evidence tab of the site under "Stress tests". All holdout numbers there are non-confirmatory.

## Checks and tolerance

```text
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python run.py test       # full pytest suite; tests write only to temporary folders
python run.py check      # same as python -m src.check
python run.py regression # re-estimate the main model in memory and compare it with the artifact; writes nothing
```

`python -m src.check` re-runs ingest, model and report in a temporary directory and compares the results with the committed files. It also re-runs the exploratory stress tests. It prints PASS, FAIL or WARN for each item (WARN only for results of optimizer runs that did not converge, which can differ slightly across platforms, and for figures whose pixels differ only through font rasterization on another operating system; see `docs/deviations.md`, D14 and D16): both processed panels, the headline scores, every coefficient, every number in `outputs/*.md`, every entry of `outputs/numbers_for_note.json`, the three figures (pixel by pixel, then on small-block averages), this README, and every file generated from the fact forms. Tolerances are stored in the artifact: 0.01 for the headline (holdout RMSE ratio and the latest policy pressure score), and 1e-06 for coefficients and every other number. The model uses a fixed random seed (42), which is also recorded in the artifact.

`python run.py regression` re-fits only the main ordered logit, in memory, on the estimation sample recorded in `model/artifact.json`, and prints one PASS or FAIL line per estimate, robust standard error and p-value (and the log-likelihood) at the coefficient tolerance 1e-06; it writes nothing and exits with code 1 if any line fails.

Acceptance checks: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_acceptance.py`. Set `KZ_SKIP_CLEAN_INSTALL=1` to skip the slow fresh-venv install. The standalone scripts are `python scripts/clean_install_check.py` and `python scripts/scan_secrets.py`.

```text
src/app.py                read-only Streamlit dashboard

model/artifact.json       fitted parameters, covariance, diagnostics, tolerances
outputs/                  generated tables, figures and annexes; outputs/legacy/ holds superseded work

scripts/                  clean-install and secret-scan checks

```

## Limitations

- **No distinguishable result against Always Hold.** The model meets the pre-specified criterion (RMSE ratio 0.995, below 1), but the difference cannot be told apart from zero, so this does not show that the model forecasts better. The 95% block-bootstrap interval for the RMSE ratio (0.780 to 1.335) contains 1, and the Diebold–Mariano test (HLN-corrected) gives p = 0.961, so on 18 holdout decisions the model cannot be distinguished from Always Hold in either direction. The holdout overlaps an earlier exploratory backtest, so it is not untouched.
- **Data update.** Interpretation of the data update: the holdout is the last 18 usable decisions (2024-09-02 to 2026-10-27); appending a decision moves the unchanged chronological split rule, so the estimation and holdout windows shift with the data. 1 of these decisions (2026-10-27) took place after the specification was dated (2026-10-16); the other 17 had already been seen in earlier runs. The holdout is therefore partly newer data but still not an untouched confirmatory holdout.
- **Next-decision forecast.** The probabilities shown for the next NBK decision are the model's probabilities at the latest decision in the data (2026-10-27), computed from its factor month 2026-08 (decision month minus 2). See `docs/deviations.md` (D21).
- **Policy inertia (exploratory).** Policy-inertia specifications (exploratory only; P0 = inflation, its 3-month change, the ex-post real rate and the previous decision; P1 = P0 plus the other five factors, ridge). RPS of the specification vs the main model M0 — P0: rolling origin inside the estimation sample 0.165 vs 0.213; fixed-origin holdout 0.220 vs 0.154; recursive holdout 0.156 vs 0.148 | P1: rolling origin inside the estimation sample 0.173 vs 0.213; fixed-origin holdout 0.254 vs 0.154; recursive holdout 0.144 vs 0.148. P0 has the lower RPS in 1 of 3 designs; P1 has the lower RPS in 2 of 3 designs. The ranking depends on the evaluation design, which is instability, not an improvement; neither specification replaces the pre-specified model.
- **Release-lag assumption.** Factors are aligned to the month two months before each decision. Actual publication lags are unknown, so the absence of look-ahead is not verified. File update dates give only upper bounds on the lags. Look-ahead cannot be excluded for 89 of 89 decisions for exports and imports (and for 15 of 89 decisions for consumption). `outputs/release_lag_check.md` lists the bounds and the decisions where possible look-ahead cannot be ruled out, and the Evidence tab of the site shows the same limitation. Alternative lags give: "Ordered logit: release lag 1 month": Always Hold (survives No); "Ordered logit: release lag 3 months": Model beats Hold (survives No).
- **Irregular decision-date sampling.** The 89 usable observations (2016-03-15 to 2026-10-27; 2 dropped for missing factors) are NBK meeting dates, not equally spaced periods. Serial-correlation and unit-root tests assume regular spacing.
- **No data vintages.** The factors are current-vintage values. Revisions after each decision date are not tracked. Publisher, source title, URL, navigation path, publication and retrieval dates are recorded where known (student statement, `data/raw/SOURCES.md`); `base_rate_history.csv` comes from a table on prg.kz that cites NBK press releases. The source pages carry no series codes, so each series is identified by its title (student statement). Release lags and revision status are UNKNOWN for every file (see `TODO_HUMAN.md`). Units are recorded in `docs/facts_to_fill.csv` (student statement) and compared with the CSV column names in `docs/data_audit.md`; conflicts are reported there, not resolved. Trade is in USD and lending in KZT, so the growth rates of these series also carry exchange-rate and price effects.
- **Household lending is non-stationary.** For the transformed series, ADF does not reject a unit root (p 0.133) and KPSS rejects stationarity (reported p 0.010, the bound of the KPSS lookup table). The one significant slope therefore rests on a series that fails both tests. Differencing it in "Differenced non-stationary factors" gives: survives No; same signs no; benchmark conclusion Model beats Hold.
- **Parameter instability.** A likelihood-ratio test of equal slopes in the earlier and later parts of the estimation sample rejects stability (p 0.013; flag FAIL; 31 and 40 decisions; the split is recorded in the artifact).
- **Small sample.** 71 estimation and 18 holdout decisions. The holdout contains 3 increases and 4 decreases.

## Declared borrowing

| What is reused | From | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Ordered logit estimator (`OrderedModel`) | statsmodels | `src/model.py` |
| Holm adjustment (`multipletests`), ADF and KPSS (`adfuller`, `kpss`), Ljung–Box (`acorr_ljungbox`), VIF (`variance_inflation_factor`) | statsmodels | `src/model.py` |
| Chi-square and normal distributions | SciPy | `src/model.py` |
| Data handling | pandas, NumPy | all modules |
| Dashboard and its test harness (`AppTest`) | Streamlit | `src/app.py`, `tests/` |
| Figures | matplotlib | `src/report.py` |
| Logistic regression and random forest (legacy classifier only) | scikit-learn | `src/legacy_classifier.py`, `outputs/legacy/` |
| Test runner | pytest | `tests/` |
| HC0 sandwich covariance, delta method, Brant-type proportional-odds test, Holm procedure | Standard statistical methods, implemented in this repository; bibliographic references are UNKNOWN (see `TODO_HUMAN.md`) | `src/model.py`, `src/app.py` |
| Raw data files | Derived by manual cleaning from Excel files published by the Bureau of National Statistics (stat.gov.kz) and the National Bank of Kazakhstan (nationalbank.kz), per the student; titles, URLs and dates in `data/raw/SOURCES.md`. `base_rate_history.csv` comes from a secondary table on prg.kz that cites NBK press releases; the table is not an NBK publication | `data/raw/` |
| Upcoming meeting dates | The NBK decision-making schedule page linked in `config/forecast_rounds.json` | `config/forecast_rounds.json` |
| Historical decision dates | Source UNKNOWN (see `TODO_HUMAN.md`) | `config/nbk_decision_dates.csv` |
| AI assistance | An AI coding assistant was used to write and revise code and documents; the student records the details in `docs/ai_use.md` | see `docs/ai_use.md` |

Literature references are in `docs/references.md`. Exact package versions are pinned in `requirements.txt` and recorded in the artifact. Contributions are recorded in `docs/contributions.md`.

## Legacy note (superseded classifier)

> **Legacy, not a current result.** An earlier version of this project classified decisions with logistic regression and random forest classifiers and reported their accuracy against a Hold benchmark. That work is superseded by the ordered-logit indicator above and is kept only for the record in `outputs/legacy/` (see `outputs/legacy/INDEX.md`; its metrics are in `outputs/legacy/mvp_backtest_results.json`). Do not quote it as a result of this project.
